boundaries.note: No sporting route in either direction. Promotion and relegation were suspended in 2020; a CAS ruling of 4 Sep 2025 ordered their return from 2026-27, but Liga MX's new regulations (16 Jul 2026) formalised a closed league instead. Atlante's arrival in 2026-27 came from buying Mazatlán's franchise, not from promotion.

conflicts.real: none in practice, but legally contested
conflicts.note: The CAS ordered relegation back for 2026-27; Liga MX ignored it and made itself a closed league in July 2026, and the FMF's August 2026 model keeps Liga MX closed while restoring promotion between Liga de Expansión and Liga Premier. A Mexican Senate bill (Sep 2026) would force promotion back. Treat as closed for now, with political risk.
The Liga de Expansión MX article's format paragraph says '15 clubs' while its own 2026-27 participant list and infobox say 16. Used 16.

conflicts.ours: Liga MX Apertura / Liga de Expansión MX Clausura / U19 Apertura / U21 Apertura
conflicts.real: Liga MX, Liga de Expansión MX, Liga MX Sub-19, Liga MX Sub-21
conflicts.note: All four are year-round competitions split into Apertura and Clausura; the row names carry one tournament, not the competition.

notes: Two tournaments per season (Apertura Jul-Dec, Clausura Jan-May), each a single table of 17 rounds plus an eight-team liguilla. Liga MX has 18 clubs after Atlante replaced Mazatlán; 2026-27 has no promotion or relegation. The U19 and U21 categories (Fuerzas Basicas) run alongside with one side per Liga MX club, so 18 each; their Apertura 2026 calendar runs to at least matchday 18, so the exact round count is left null. Level 99 is our marker for youth competitions, not a pyramid level.
